howIntro: What the page measures, how its commentary is written and checked, what data it needs, and how it could run during a live match.
howBattery_1: Above a typical pro's critical speed, about 4.1 m/s (14.8 km/h), running drains a short-term reserve, metre for metre. Below it the reserve refills: quickly at a walk, slowly at a jog.
howBattery_2: We do not know each player's own fitness, so the page runs 200 typical professionals through the same running (critical speed 4.1 ± 0.3 m/s, reserve 180 ± 54 m) and shows their weighted median; analysts also get the 10–90% band.
howBattery_3: Why a typical pro: on synthetic matches where we know each player's true state, no method we tested could pick out a player's own low moments from positions alone (precision 0.20 at best).
howBattery_4: Each second uses only the running so far: the battery at minute 30 does not know what happens at minute 60.
howChartTitle: {name}: speed and battery, second by second
howChartSub: The opening clip's run and the eight minutes after it. Dashed: the typical pro's critical speed. Shaded: the clip's run.
howChartBattery: Battery a typical pro would have after the same running, %
howAgentsTitle: The commentary: four agents and a Verifier
howAgents_1: Plain code measures the match; the agents only explain it. They run on Microsoft Foundry (Agent Framework, gpt-5-mini) and see the match only through an MCP server with seven read-only tools, each number returned with its unit and where it came from.
howAgentStep_5: Narrator agent: writes from published claims
howAgentStep_7: Verifier: rules, then an LLM that can only block
howAgents_2: The Verifier checks every sentence before it reaches the page, against a register of claims taken from published research and against the moment's own numbers. On 192 test sentences:
howAgents_3: The LLM pass varies from run to run, so it is a second net, not a guarantee; the rules give the same verdict every time.
howData_1: Player and ball positions, 10 times a second (optical or broadcast tracking).
howData_3: Whether the ball is in play and who has it, and events (passes, turnovers, shots) for some moments, such as a team caught on the break.
howData_4: Not needed: wearables, GPS vests or fitness tests. The battery is a typical pro's.
howDataSynthetic: Every match here is synthetic: a generator built from published sports science, with a hidden true state we use to test the estimator. Its movement is checked against real tracking (IDSSE, SkillCorner, Metrica) and Wyscout's Premier League events.
howLiveIntro: The site replays files. This is how the same parts could run live; we have not built or tested it.
howLive_1: Tracking feed: positions arrive 10 times a second.
howLive_2: Speed: the replay smooths each half looking both ways; live, the filter can only look back, which adds a short delay.
howLive_3: Battery: it already uses only the running so far, so it updates every second.
howLive_4: Moments: each is found when its window closes, such as his hardest minutes or a second wind.
howLive_5: Agents and Verifier: each line needs model calls, so it arrives after its moment, not with it.
howLive_6: Overlay: lines and batteries pushed to the broadcast through a stream (Azure Event Hubs was planned, and cut for the hackathon).
